Rashi on Eruvin 105a:10:1.hebrew: קושרה - בנימת כנור שנפסקה. ופליג רבי שמעון ואמר בברייתא: עונבה, ואמר הכא טעמא למילתא, ופליג אתנא דלעיל, ואמר: לא הותרו במקדש אלא שבות. ובתרתי מיפלגא מילתא דרבי שמעון: רישא — במחשיך חוץ לתחום, וסיפא — בנימת כנור. והכי קאמר רבי שמעון לתנא קמא: אע"פ שהקלתי במחשיך חוץ לתחום, מחמיר אני בנימת כנור, דהתם משלך נתנו לך, אבל כאן לא התירו אלא שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:10:1.english: One ties it - [This refers to] a harp string that snapped. And Rabbi Shimon disagrees and states in a baraita: One [only] forms a bow; and here [in our mishnah] he stated the reason for the matter, and he disagrees with the tanna [mentioned] above and said: Only [activities prohibited due to] a rabbinic decree were permitted in the Temple. And Rabbi Shimon's statement is divided into two [parts]: the first part [deals with] one overtaken by darkness outside the [Shabbat] limit, and the concluding part [deals with] a harp string. And this is what Rabbi Shimon is saying to the first tanna: "Even though I was lenient in [the case of] one overtaken by darkness outside the limit, I am stringent regarding a harp string; for there, they gave you [only] from your own, but here, they permitted only [activities prohibited due to] a rabbinic decree."

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:11:1.hebrew: קשירה דאתיא לידי חיוב חטאת - במדינה, גזרה שמא יקשור קשר של קיימא:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:11:1.english: Tying, which leads to liability for a sin-offering - In the provinces; [it is a] decree lest one tie a permanent knot.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יוחנן - לענין עיולי, כולי עלמא המכניס שרץ חייב. ולענין להוציא הנמצא בעזרה בשבת — בהאי קרא פליגי:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said - With regard to bringing [it] in, everyone agrees that one who brings in a creeping animal is liable. And with regard to removing [one] found in the courtyard on Shabbat, they disagree over this verse:

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:2.hebrew: ויבאו הכהנים פנימי בית ה' בהיכל ויוציאו הטומאה - ע"ז ותקרובתיה, שהן מטמאין באהל:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:2.english: “And the priests went into the inner part of the House of the Lord... in the Temple, and they brought out the impurity” - [This refers to] idolatry and its offerings, which transmit impurity in a tent.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:3.english: Into the courtyard of the House of the Lord - [This is the] Temple courtyard [the Azarah].

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:4.hebrew: ויקבלו הלוים להוציא משם לנחל קדרון - אבל כהנים אחרים לא מיטמאין, אע"פ שהיו צריכים לאנשים הרבה. אלו מוציאין מן ההיכל לעזרה, ואילו משם ולחוץ — לוים הוא דמיטמאין, ולא כהנים. בן ננס סבר: מדאשתני טומאת עזרה מכהנים ללוים, שמע מינה: היכא דאיתא בעזרה לא מפקינן ליה בעבירה, אלא מהדרינן אהתירא; ובשבת נמי לא דחינן שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:1:4.english: And the Levites took it to carry it out from there to the brook of Kidron - But other priests would not defile themselves, even though they needed many people. These [priests] would bring [it] out from the Sanctuary to the courtyard, whereas from there outward, it was Levites who would defile themselves, and not priests. Ben Nannas reasoned: Since [the removal of] impurity in the courtyard shifted from priests to Levites, conclude from this: Wherever it is in the courtyard, we do not remove it through a transgression, but rather we seek a permitted [way]; and on Shabbat as well, we do not override a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:2:1.hebrew: טומאה בעזרה ליתא - כלומר, היכא דאיתא התם, לא חמירא כולי האי:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:2:1.english: There is no impurity in the courtyard - That is to say, where it is [found] there, it is not so severe.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:3:1.hebrew: דלא אפשר - בהיכל לא עיילי לוים, דאפי' כהנים אסירי למיעל אלא לעבודה, כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:ב׳) "ואל יבא בכל עת אל הקדש" — זה היכל, "מבית לפרוכת" — זה לפני ולפנים:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:3:1.english: Where it is impossible - Into the Sanctuary of the Temple, Levites do not enter, as even priests are forbidden to enter except for service, as it is written (Leviticus 16:2): "That he come not at all times into the holy place" — this is the Sanctuary; "within the veil" — this is the Holy of Holies.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:3:2.hebrew: תו לא מטמאינן לכהנים - שהרי אפשר בלוים, אבל לשהויי עד אורתא — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:3:2.english: We no longer render priests ritually impure - For it is possible [to do so] with Levites; but to leave [it] until the evening [is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:5:1.hebrew: מסייע כהני - דאמר לקמן, כהנים טמאין עדיפי מטהורי ישראלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:5:1.english: Supports priests - For he says below that impure priests take precedence over pure Israelites.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:5:2.english: “Only he shall not go in unto the veil,” etc. - It is written regarding [priests] with blemishes.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:5:3.english: Beaten plates - Sheets of gold with which they overlay the Holy of Holies from within.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:6:1.hebrew: אך חלק - כלומר: אכין ורקין מיעוטין, כל אתין וגמין רבויין. חלק — מיעט, דלמלאכה שרי לעיולי:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:6:1.english: “Only” — it made a distinction - That is to say, [the words] *akh* and *rak* are exclusions, [while] all [words] *et* and *gam* are inclusions. “It made a distinction” — it excluded [from the prohibition], [meaning] that for work it is permitted to enter.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:1.hebrew: טמא ובעל מום - אי אפשר אלא באחד מהן, איזה מהן מכניסין:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:1.english: An impure [priest] and a blemished [priest] - [If] it is impossible [to do so] except with one of them, which of them do we bring in?

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:2.hebrew: דהא אישתרי בעבודת צבור - דכתיב (במדבר כח) "במועדו" — ואפילו בטומאה. אבל בעל מום לא הותר, דתניא בתורת כהנים: "מום בו את לחם אלהיו לא יגש להקריב" — אין לי אלא תמידין, שהן קרויין לחם, כענין שנאמר: "את קרבני לחמי לאשי"; שאר קרבנות צבור מנין? ת"ל שוב "לחם". קרא אחרינא, וכתיב בתריה: "לחם אלהיו מקדשי הקדשים", וסמיך ליה אקרא קמא, דנשתמע הכי: "לא יגש להקריב לחם אלהיו":
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:2.english: As he is permitted in communal service - For it is written (Numbers 28:2): "In its appointed season" — and [this means] even in ritual impurity. However, a blemished [priest] was not permitted, as it is taught in Torat Kohanim: "[Because] he has a blemish, he shall not approach to offer the bread of his God" (Leviticus 21:21) — I have [derived] only the daily offerings, which are called "bread," as the matter is stated: "My offering, My bread for My fire offerings" (Numbers 28:2); from where [do I derive] the other communal sacrifices? The verse states "bread" again. [This refers to] another verse, as it is written after it: "The bread of his God, of the most holy [sacrifices...]" (Leviticus 21:22); and [the exposition] links it to the first verse, so that it may be understood as follows: "He shall not approach to offer the bread of his God."

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:3.hebrew: דהא אישתרי באכילת קדשים - מהאי קרא: "לחם אלהיו מקדשי הקדשים ומן הקדשים יאכל":
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:7:3.english: As he is permitted to eat consecrated foods - From this verse: "He may eat the bread of his God, of the most holy and of the holy."

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:8:1.english: The surveyors - [They] measure the [Shabbat] limits and set up a marker when they measure their measurement.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:8:2.hebrew: מפני טועי המדה - שמא יטעו בה, הלכך מקצרין אותה. נמצא שעדיין התחום לא הגיע, ומי שהחשיך לו חוץ לתחום — כבר נכנס בתוך אלפים ט"ו אמות, כדפרישית במי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף נב.). ל"א: מפני הטועין — ששוכחין ויוצאין, וחוזרין ונכנסין. לפיכך מקצרין המודדין את התחום, הסימן, ומציבין בתוך התחום, שאם יצא לא עביד איסורא:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:8:2.english: Because of those who err in the measurement - Lest they err in [measuring] it; therefore, they shorten it. Consequently, the [actual] boundary has not yet been reached [at the marker], and one for whom it grew dark outside the boundary [marker] has already entered within the two thousand [cubits by these] fifteen cubits, as I explained in [the chapter entitled] *Mi SheHotzi’uhu* (above, Eruvin 52b). Another explanation: "Because of those who err" — [this refers to those] who forget and go out, and turn back and re-enter. Therefore, the surveyors shorten the boundary [marker], the sign, and erect [it] within the boundary, so that if one goes out, he has not committed a transgression.

Rashi on Eruvin 105a:9:1.hebrew: יכנס - דמשלך נתנו לך, שכבר הוא בתוך תחומו. והכא אתא ר' שמעון למיתב טעמא למילתיה: דלא תימא מיקל אני באיסור שבת, אלא משלו נתתי לו. והכא נקט לה משום פלוגתא דנימת כנור, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Eruvin 105a:9:1.english: He may enter - For "they granted you from your own," as he is already within his [Shabbat] limit. And here, Rabbi Shimon came to give the reason for his statement [there]: so that you should not say, "I am lenient regarding the prohibition of Shabbat"; rather, "I have given him of his own." And here, [the Mishnah] cited it because of the dispute concerning the harp string, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain.

Tosafot on Eruvin 105a:1:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יוחנן ושניהם מקרא אחד דרשו - פירש בקונטרס שבא לתרץ, דכולי עלמא מכניס שרץ חייב, ולענין הוצאת טומאה פליגי. ותימה, דלכאורה אין חילוק; דאי מכניס שרץ חייב, הוא הדין דמוזהר להוציא מ"וישלחו מן המחנה" — דכל היכא דקרינן "לא יטמאו את משכני", קרינן "וישלחו". וא"כ, מאי טעמא דמאן דאמר "מעזרה לא"? ונראה, דמילתא באפי נפשה היא, ולא קאי לדחויי הא דקאמר לעיל "כתנאי", ופליג בין במכניס בין במוציא — דאין חילוק כדפירשנו — אלא בא לאסמוכי קרא למאן דאמר חייב ולמאן דאמר פטור:
Tosafot on Eruvin 105a:1:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And both of them derived [their opinions from] the same verse - The Kuntres explained that [Rabbi Yoḥanan] comes to resolve [the discussion, establishing] that everyone agrees that one who brings a creeping animal [into the Temple] is liable, and they disagree regarding the removal of impurity. And this is astonishing, for apparently there is no distinction; for if one who brings in a creeping animal is liable, the same applies that he is commanded to remove [it], from: “That they put out of the camp” (Numbers 5:2) — for wherever we apply: “That they defile not My Tabernacle,” we apply: “That they put out.” And if so, what is the reasoning of the one who says [that it is] not [removed] from the courtyard? And it appears that [Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement] is an independent matter, and does not stand to reject that which [the Gemara] said above, “Is it a dispute between tanna’im?” — and [indeed] the dispute is both regarding one who brings [it] in and regarding one who removes [it], for there is no distinction, as we explained; rather, [Rabbi Yoḥanan] came to provide scriptural support for the one who says [he is] liable and for the one who says [he is] exempt.

Tosafot on Eruvin 105a:9:1.hebrew: אמר ר' שמעון יכנס - והכי קאמר ליה רבי שמעון לתנא קמא: אע"פ שמיקל אני במחשיך חוץ לתחום, מחמיר אני בנימת הכנור — דהתם לאו קולא הוא, אלא משלך נתנו לך; וגם כאן, לא נתנו לך אלא משלך, דהיינו עניבה, דהוה דבר המותר. והא דנטר עד הכא — משום דבעי לאסוקי מילי דבמקדש אבל לא במדינה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 105a:9:1.english: Rabbi Shimon said: He may enter - And this is what Rabbi Shimon is saying to the first tanna: Even though I am lenient regarding one for whom it grew dark outside the [Shabbat] limit, I am stringent regarding the harp string. For there, it is not a leniency, but rather "from your own they gave to you"; and here too, they gave you only from your own, that is, looping, which is an inherently permitted act. And as for the fact that [the Tanna] waited until here [to state this] — [it is] because he wanted to conclude the matters [permitted] in the Temple but not in the rest of the country.
